title: Middle East conflict extension cuts global Q4 2026 crude run forecast by 1.4 million b/d
gist: Wood Mackenzie cuts its Q4 2026 global crude run forecast by 1.4 million b/d on an extended Middle East conflict plus Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries, arguing current elevated Asian refining margins are a temporary windfall masking a structural shift toward a sub-$60 Brent, peak-demand world where only deeply chemical-integrated, energy-efficient refiners (increasingly Chinese) will remain competitive.

themes.theme: Scale and drivers of the refining disruption

insights.claim: Extending the Middle East conflict to year-end is estimated to cut global crude runs by 1.4 million barrels per day in Q4 2026, with Asia bearing the brunt of the reduction.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A 1.4 million b/d Q4 crude-run cut is a concrete input for modeling refined-product supply tightness and refining-margin direction into year-end.

insights.claim: Persistent Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries have compounded the Middle East-driven disruption, with Russian refinery unit outages reaching 3.5 million b/d in August, further tightening the global refining system.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Two independent geopolitical shocks (Middle East conflict and Ukraine drone campaign) are compounding rather than offsetting, a reason global refining tightness could persist longer than a single-conflict resolution would suggest.
insights.locator: Persistent Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries have compounded the disruption

insights.claim: The current scale of disruption to global crude runs is without modern precedent, according to Wood Mackenzie's SVP of refining, chemicals and oil markets research.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Framing this as historically unprecedented signals investors should not simply mean-revert to pre-conflict refining-margin assumptions.
insights.quote: The scale of disruption to global crude runs is without modern precedent

themes.theme: Margins today versus a $50-60 Brent world ahead

insights.claim: The Middle East and Russia/Ukraine conflicts have limited crude runs and driven refining margins to elevated levels across the region, prompting US and European refiners to defer scheduled maintenance into 2027.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Deferred maintenance into 2027 implies refiners are extending run rates now to capture windfall margins, a signal to watch for a maintenance-driven margin pullback next year.
insights.locator: US and European refiners deferring scheduled maintenance into 2027

insights.claim: Diesel markets remain strong due to Russian export constraints, continued inventory reductions, and rising winter heating demand, while gasoline prices are likely to ease seasonally but stay supported by limited Atlantic Basin supply through year-end.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Diesel cracks are the stronger near-term long relative to gasoline given the specific supply constraints named here.
insights.locator: diesel markets remain strong due to Russian export constraints

insights.claim: Once Strait of Hormuz flows are fully restored and non-OPEC production growth exceeds global demand growth in 2027 and 2028, Wood Mackenzie forecasts Dated Brent will decline to a $50-60 per barrel range.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A specific $50-60/bbl post-restoration Brent target gives investors a numeric anchor for the eventual downside once the current geopolitical premium unwinds.
insights.locator: Wood Mackenzie forecasts Dated Brent will decline to the $50-60 per barrel range

insights.claim: Refiners should treat today's elevated margin windfall as a down payment on transformation, since a lower oil-price environment combined with approaching peak oil demand will quickly expose the gap between competitive and uncompetitive refining assets.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Windfall refining cash flow should be judged by whether it is being redeployed into competitiveness (integration, efficiency) versus simply distributed, since the current margin environment is explicitly framed as temporary.
insights.quote: Refiners must treat today’s windfall as a down payment on transformation

themes.theme: Asian demand scarring and recovery divergence

insights.claim: Asia Pacific oil demand is not expected to return to pre-conflict levels until late 2027, following a projected 1.24 million b/d decline in 2026, with petrochemical feedstocks (LPG and naphtha) hit hardest and road fuels proving more resilient.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A near two-year demand-recovery lag with feedstock-specific scarring points to petrochemical-linked demand as the weakest link in Asian oil markets, not transport fuel.
insights.locator: Asia Pacific oil demand is not expected to return to pre-conflict levels until late 2027

insights.claim: India is leading the regional oil demand recovery and will be the first market to surpass pre-conflict demand levels, with Southeast Asia following, while China's oil demand likely peaked before the conflict even began.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: India is the clear relative-growth story in Asian oil demand, while China is flagged as already past peak demand — a structural, not conflict-driven, divergence.
insights.locator: India is leading the regional recovery

themes.theme: Structural shift in Asia's crude supply base

insights.claim: Middle East crude production is recovering, aided by shuttle transits and ship-to-ship transfers that have made the blockade less effective than initially expected, while China's pace of strategic-inventory rebuilding remains a key uncertainty for price forecasts.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: China's inventory rebuild pace is flagged explicitly as a swing factor for crude price forecasts — a variable worth monitoring directly.
insights.locator: Middle East crude production is recovering, supported by shuttle transits

insights.claim: Asia's crude import dependency is expected to reach 82%, with an additional 1.5 million b/d of imports by 2030, shifting the supply mix toward long-haul barrels from the US and Latin America as the Middle East's share of Asian crude imports declines from over 65% today.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A structural pivot of Asian crude sourcing toward US/Latin American long-haul barrels is a multi-year tailwind for those exporters and for tanker/freight demand on longer routes.
insights.locator: Asia's crude import dependency is expected to reach 82%

insights.claim: The conflict has accelerated the structural diversification of Asia's crude supply base, and refiners able to optimise across a wider crude slate — particularly grades with higher middle-distillate yields — will be best positioned to capture value in this evolving environment.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Refiners with feedstock flexibility (not tied to Middle East grades) are the structural winners as Asia's crude sourcing diversifies.
insights.quote: The conflict has accelerated the structural diversification of Asia’s crude supply base

themes.theme: Refinery competitiveness: integration and efficiency as decisive levers

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's Refinery Evaluation Model shows deep chemical integration is the primary margin driver for Asian refiners, with second-generation integrated sites achieving chemical yields above 40% and much higher net cash margins than first-generation sites; partial integration is not sufficient for first-quartile competitiveness.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Investors evaluating Asian refining/petrochemical assets should screen for chemical-yield thresholds (>40%) as a competitiveness cutoff, not just integration in name.
insights.locator: Wood Mackenzie's Refinery Evaluation Model highlights deep chemical integration

insights.claim: By 2035, nearly 80% of top-performing refineries are expected to be Chinese assets with extensive chemical integration.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: China is positioned to dominate the top tier of global refining competitiveness by 2035, a long-horizon thesis for capital allocation in Asian downstream oil and chemicals.
insights.locator: by 2035, nearly 80% of top-performing refineries are expected to be Chinese assets

insights.claim: About 55% of refineries currently exceed the global benchmark for energy intensity, and the least competitive refineries tend to also have higher energy intensity, making efficiency investment essential for both margins and sustainability.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Energy-intensity data offers a screenable, quantifiable proxy for identifying which refining assets are most at risk of falling out of competitiveness.
insights.locator: about 55% of refineries exceed the global benchmark for energy intensity

insights.claim: For many refiners, import substitution and margin competitiveness amount to the same investment decision, meaning global peers are actively reshaping portfolios in response to the changing environment.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Frames refining capex decisions as dual-purpose (defending domestic market share and margin) — useful lens for evaluating refiners' capital-allocation announcements.
insights.quote: For many refiners, import substitution and margin competitiveness are the same investment decision.
insights.locator: quote from Alan Gelder, looking ahead to 2035 outlook
